title: Correction for Bernabé-Rubio and Watt, Caspase-8-dependent autophagy regulates neutrophil infiltration in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
Beyond $χ^2$: Ensemble null tests for reliable scientific discovery
summary: Unrecognized systematic errors can survive standard checks and undermine scientific discoveries. Null tests and experimental controls can expose these failures, but averaging measurements or reducing them to scalar statistics can hide important structure. We propose ensemble null tests that compare multivariate distributions with references from observations or simulations. We demonstrate their benefits across science. In cosmic microwave background simulations, they detect systematic effects missed by conventional $χ^2$ tests. In Gaia data, they detect velocity asymmetry as sensitively as an informed search. In a CRISPR screen, they expose a control mismatch in DNA damage and reveal which cellular profiles drive it. As scientific datasets grow, ensemble testing turns repeated measurements into a broader search for unknown unknowns, strengthening the empirical foundation for scientific discovery.

title: The RNA m6A reader YTHDF2 depletion phenocopies high glucose induced-cellular stress response in diabetic kidney disease
summary: RNA modification, especially the m6A RNA methylation, has been increasingly associated with several physiological and pathophysiological processes. The proteins that help in establishment of the modification and its removal along with the reader proteins that facilitate the functional outcome, together play an important regulatory role in disease manifestation. Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is one such example, which is categorized as a multifactorial disorder that involves complex metabolic, oxidative, inflammatory, and fibrotic alterations, mediated through genetic, epigenetic and signalling cascades. However, the contribution of m6A-associated RNA regulators in DKD manifestation is relatively less explored. In this study, using HFD+STZ-induced diabetic mice and high glucose-treated renal cell models, we identified the m6A reader protein, Ythdf2 as a consistently downregulated candidate. YTHDF2 depletion in the renal cell line altered cellular viability, proliferation and increased oxidative stress under high-glucose conditions. Click-IT EU labeling further revealed altered RNA processing effects following YTHDF2 depletion and glucose stress. In corroboration with the above observations in animal and cell line models, independent human DKD transcriptomic datasets demonstrated conserved inflammatory and fibrotic signatures as well as reduced YTHDF2 expression in DKD glomeruli. The YTHDF2 downregulation was found to be inversely correlated with several disease-associated inflammatory and fibrotic genes. Together, these findings identify YTHDF2 dysregulation as a potential post-transcriptional mechanism associated with cellular stress and disease-associated molecular programs in DKD.

title: Mechanistic insights into proteolytic activation ofmembrane-bound NAC transcription factor SlNACMTF3 intomato plants under heat stress
summary: Stress is perceived at the cellular membrane, where membrane-bound transcription factors (MTFs) are activated, initiating a rapid gene-regulation cascade. We previously demonstrated the multifaceted role of tomato MTF, SlNACMTF3, in regulating expression of biotic and abiotic stress responsive genes. However, the molecular mechanism underlying its activation following stress perception remained unknown. Here, we show that the membrane rhomboid protease SlRP3 recognizes an ISK motif near the transmembrane domain of SlNACMTF3 for cleavage and releasing the transcription factor from the membrane. SlRP3 and SlNACMTF3 co-localize within the same plasma membrane microdomain and interact directly. Molecular dynamics simulations supported the proposed mechanism, in which heat-induced conformational switching of SlRP3, driven by reorientation of the L5 loop, enhances substrate accessibility and proteolytic activity. Furthermore, mutation of key SlRP3 residues involved in substrate interaction impaired SlNACMTF3 activation and reduced the expression of stress33 responsive genes. Analysis with SlNACMTF3-overexpressing tomato lines and SlRP3 transient knockdown leaves further revealed that transcription factor activation, stress35 responsive gene regulation, and cellular ROS detoxification occur coordinately. Collectively, these findings provide mechanistic insight into stress-triggered SlNACMTF3 activation and identify SlRP3 as a novel membrane-associated stress sensor that activates a major transcriptional regulator to enhance stress preparedness in economically important tomato plants.

title: A specialized SUV3 RNA helicase is involved in plant mitochondrial DNA repair
summary: Synonymous substitution rates in the coding regions of land plant mitochondrial genomes are substantially lower than those in the nucleus. In contrast, non-coding regions are difficult or impossible to align except among very closely related species, suggesting that point mutation rates in these regions are considerably higher. Rearrangement breakpoints occur frequently within non-coding DNA, generating duplications, deletions, and inversions. To reconcile these contradictory patterns of genome evolution, it has been proposed that DNA damage is converted into double-strand breaks that are repaired through a combination of template-directed mechanisms and non-homologous end joining, while purifying selection preserves the integrity of coding sequences. Here we characterized AtSUV3, a mitochondrially targeted RNA helicase encoded by Arabidopsis thaliana At4g14790, a gene previously proposed to function as part of the plant mitochondrial degradosome. Mutations in AtSUV3 confer hypersensitivity to ciprofloxacin-induced mitochondrial DNA damage, CRISPR- knockout lines display increased ectopic recombination in the mitochondrial genome, and recombinant AtSUV3 exhibits ATP-dependent RNA helicase activity with a preference for 3'-ended substrates. Together, these findings identify AtSUV3 as a factor involved in mitochondrial dsDNA break repair. Consistent with our results, Arabidopsis and other plants encode an uncharacterized gene, AT5G39840.1, with 75% amino acid similarity with AtSUV3, dubbed herein as SUV3-like. We hypothesize that the AtSUV3 paralog has undergone specialization towards DNA repair, whereas AtSUV3-like protein may play a role in the plant organellar degradosome. Collectively, these findings identify AtSUV3 as a previously unrecognized factor involved in mitochondrial dsDNA break repair and provide a framework for understanding the diversification of DNA repair proteins during plant evolution.

title: Epigenetic clocks and nonlinear aging in Odocoileus deer
summary: Population age structure has important consequences for population dynamics and is a key parameter for wildlife demography and management. Epigenetic clocks have emerged as accurate molecular tools for estimating chronological age. Ungulates are among the most intensively managed wildlife worldwide, yet epigenetic clocks have been developed for only two cervid species. Here, we develop a novel epigenetic clock for mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus) and a multi-species clock for the Odocoileus genus, and use them to investigate variation in age-associated DNA methylation across the mule deer lifespan. The mule deer clock achieved accuracy comparable to recently developed mammalian epigenetic clocks (r {approx} 0.9; MAE {approx} 5% of species lifespan). The multi-species Odocoileus clock showed lower predictive performance (r = 0.72; MAE = 0.782 years), but its broader taxonomic applicability may be particularly valuable where Odocoileus species occur sympatrically and hybridize. Cross-sectional epigenetic age estimates supported nonlinear age-associated methylation dynamics across the mule deer lifespan, whereas longitudinal changes in epigenetic age indicated that clocks optimized for cross-sectional age estimation may lack sufficient resolution to quantify short-term within-individual changes. Overall, our results highlight the value of integrating clock-level, CpG-level, and longitudinal analyses to investigate aging in wild populations. We also identify strongly age-associated loci that provide candidates for developing targeted, scalable, and lower-cost assays.
